derivedForeignPowerVocabulary.method: Exact, documented lookup of the unmodified raw Foreign_Po string; this is not an administration-type field.

methodologicalWarning: These are monthly analytical boundary snapshots, not comprehensive front lines and not an explicit civil/military administration dataset. Name, Foreign_Po, Head_of_St and Govt_in_Ex are preserved as supplied. Head_of_St can identify a de facto authority rather than a constitutional head of state. October 1944–May 1945 is limited/static evidence.

processing.geometryRepairPolicy: Invalid geometries are detected, reported and repaired with Shapely make_valid before polygon-only clipping; source files are unchanged.
processing.regionalScope: Romania, Moldova, Transnistria, western Ukraine and the Southern Bug research region

projection.transformationDefinition: proj=pipeline step inv proj=aea lat_0=30 lon_0=10 lat_1=43 lat_2=62 x_0=0 y_0=0 ellps=intl step proj=push v_3 step proj=cart ellps=intl step proj=helmert x=-87 y=-98 z=-121 step inv proj=cart ellps=WGS84 step proj=pop v_3 step proj=unitconvert xy_in=rad xy_out=deg
projection.transformationDescription: Inverse of Europe_Albers_Equal_Area_Conic + ED50 to WGS 84 (1) + axis order change (2D)

source.attribution: European Borders during World War II (Stanford Spatial History Lab / Holocaust Geographies Project; Michael De Groot and Erik Steiner). Derived regional adaptation by Dosare Dorohoi.
source.title: European Borders during World War II, 1938–1945
source.useLimit: Reuse and adaptation are encouraged for scholarly work. Commercial use is strictly prohibited. The source metadata asks users to inform the authors of adaptations or quality improvements.

limitedStatic.reason: The source project reports incomplete military-front data. October 1944 through April 1945 reuse the September 1944 shapefile geometry byte-for-byte; May 1945 changes geometry but remains subject to the same frontline limitation.
